likelyCause.summary: VDI login failures following a corporate AD password change are often caused by cached credentials in existing VDI sessions and potential AD account locks due to repeated authentication failures. The user having an existing VDI session open before the password change without fully signing out can cause login issues. The AD account may be locked, which IT Support can verify but cannot resolve without escalation. These conditions match the historical incident and troubleshooting guidance at Example Manufacturing.

citations.quote: Synthetic incident at Example Manufacturing. Several users could not access VDI after changing their corporate AD password. Existing VDI sessions used cached credentials. Some affected users had locked AD accounts. Support verified the account lock status and asked users to fully sign out of existing VDI sessions, then reauthenticate with the updated password. Unresolved cases were escalated to Identity Support. This historical incident does not confirm the cause of a new user's issue.

Synthetic VDI support guide for Example Manufacturing. For VDI login failure following a corporate AD password change: IT Support checks AD account lock status without modifying the account. Ask the user to save any work they can access, then fully sign out of the existing VDI session. Ask the user to reauthenticate using the updated password. If the issue persists, IT Support verifies credential synchronization status without changing account settings. Escalate unresolved cases to Identity Support. This guide does not authorize account unlocking, credential disclosure, privilege changes, or security control bypasses.

Synthetic IAM policy for Example Manufacturing. Repeated authentication failures may cause an AD account lock, including failures during VDI login after a password reset. IT Support may check account lock status. Only an authorized administrator may perform account modifications or privileged access changes. This decision-support platform must not modify accounts, unlock accounts, change privileges, or bypass authentication controls. This policy does not specify lockout thresholds or synchronization timing.

Save any accessible work, then fully sign out of the existing VDI session.
